meta.title: Position-Independent Data
meta.subtitle: Every pointer inside a blob is an offset from its own address, so the block is valid wherever it lands

views.label: Built once, in scratch
views.note: You allocate wherever it fits, then the whole graph is flattened into one contiguous allocation.

views.label: The trick, in one line
views.note: A blob pointer is a signed offset from the address of the offset field itself. Nothing in the block knows where it lives.

views.label: Written byte for byte
views.note: Because no pointer inside is absolute, serialization is a copy and deserialization is a copy back.

views.label: One word of fixup
views.note: Only the handle on the component is patched. The body is never walked, which is what makes mapping it viable.

cards.title: The one line that makes it work
items: A blob pointer stores a signed offset, not an address · Blobs.cs:737
Dereferencing takes the address of the offset field and adds the offset to it · Blobs.cs:764
A blob array does exactly the same thing for its elements · Blobs.cs:823
So the block is correct at any base address, and copying it needs no fixup at all

cards.title: What the header is for
items: A fixed thirty-two byte header sits immediately before the data · Blobs.cs:195
It carries a validation pointer, the length, the allocator and a hash · :198 to :201
The validation pointer is what turns use-after-dispose into an assert instead of garbage
For a serialized blob it is written as null and filled in on load · :208

cards.title: Load is one word per reference
items: In the file, the handle on each component is stored as a byte offset into the batch
On load the offset is replaced by the batch base plus that offset · Serialization/SerializeUtility.cs:400 to :404
Minus one is the null sentinel and stays null
Nothing walks inside the block, so the fixup cost is independent of how big the blob is

cards.title: What this buys you
items: A million entities can share one navigation mesh or one lookup table with no duplication
The block is immutable by contract, so every job can read it with no synchronisation
Blob-only types are marked so the compiler refuses to let you copy one out by value
Copy a blob field out by value and every offset inside it now points at nothing
